title: The Basie band's European tour
summary: Gus lists Marshall Royal as straw boss and trumpeters Joe Newman and Thad Jones on the 1953 England trip.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. Well, that was good. So is that the band that Basie took to Europe?
Yes, he came to Europe with that band. Marshall Royal was in the band, when we came there.
Yeah.
And I think Jaws was with us, too.
Well, Marshall was straw boss.
Yes, that's right. He was the straw boss.
Yeah. And who were those trumpets, then? Was Ernie -- no, Joe Newman?
Joe Newman was in the band.
And Thad Jones.
There was a Jones in there, a little short cat.
Oh, Jonesie or -- (Reunald Jones--ed)
Jonesie, Little Jonesie. The one that played the sweet trumpet. He's not in the band now. He lives out in California. He's an insurance worker.
Oh, is that right?
And --
(Wendell Culley)
Yeah, there was someone else that took the solos along with -- Sweets wasn't back with the band, was he?
No, Sweets -- no, no, no, not Sweets.
Somebody besides Joe Newman. Afterwards, Joe Newman and Thad Jones were in the band for a long time.
Yeah, Thad Jones came in the band before I left the band.
(Inaudible), weren't they?
Yeah.
Well, never mind, it doesn't matter. Well, so that was like about '52, '53 that you came to England.
Yes, uh-huh.
